title: SynthID assignment program output
description: The program prints one JSON object on stdout. Which shape it takes depends on the mode it was run in: --generate produces a document, --detect produces a calibrated verdict for every document it was given.

seed.description: The --seed the run was given. The same seed and the same settings must always produce the same tokens.

watermarked.description: False when --no-watermark was given: the token is then drawn straight from the model.

tokens.description: The generated document, in order. Exactly --length of them.

alpha.description: The false-positive rate the threshold was calibrated for.

bloom.description: Present only when --bloom-bits was given: the detector then used a Bloom filter in place of the exact seen-set.

calibration.description: What the unwatermarked calibration corpus produced.

threshold.description: The smallest numerator k whose tail is within alpha. A document is flagged when its numerator is at least this.

documents.description: One entry per document in --documents, in file order.

scorable.description: How many positions were scored: past the first h, context not seen before.

numerator.description: The integer k: g-values summed over scored positions and layers.

score.description: k / (layers * scorable), or 0 when nothing was scorable.

flagged.description: 1 when the numerator reaches the threshold.

false_skips.description: Present only under --bloom-bits: positions the exact set would have scored and the filter skipped.

flagged.description: How many of the documents the detector flagged: the count whose numerator reached the threshold. Turning that count into a rate needs something the detector does not know, namely whether the documents really are watermarked. On input that is all unwatermarked it is the false-positive rate; on input that is all watermarked, the true-positive rate; on mixed input such as mystery.txt it is neither, just a tally of verdicts.
